claim.why_it_matters: These subsections are emitted at the same markdown level as their own parent A.4 and as '## Annex A' / '## Annex B', so any generated table of contents or section-tree walk makes A.4.4-A.4.7 peers of the annexes rather than children of A.4, while their siblings A.4.1/A.4.2/A.4.12-A.4.14 are correctly at level 3. The run of wrongly-levelled headings is A.4.3 through A.4.11 (lines 39929-40035); A.4.4-A.4.7 are the part of that run printed on this page.

verdict.reasoning: Both quotations are accurate, but the finding is not a content discrepancy and its stated kind is wrong. WHAT I VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. (1) PDF page 1006 (printed p.976), rendered at 300dpi: the page carries exactly four bold headings - 'A.4.4 Dynamic capacity tables', 'A.4.5 DYNAMIC LENGTH elementary items', 'A.4.6 Extended letters', 'A.4.7 File sharing and record locking' - each followed by its numbered list. Confirmed. (2) The markdown page-1006 slice emits all four as level-2 '## A.4.4 ...' etc. Confirmed, each preceded by its own '' anchor. (3) The heading levels in specs/ISO_COBOL.md are exactly as quoted: '## A.4 Optional language element list' (39846), '### A.4.1 General' (39849), '### A.4.2 ...' (39864), then '## A.4.3' (39929) through '## A.4.11' (40035), then '### A.4.12' (40103), '### A.4.13' (40108), '### A.4.14' (40115). '## Annex A' (38875) and '## Annex B' (40146) are level 2. WHY I REFUTE IT. (a) NOTHING IS MISSING. kind='missing-heading' is factually wrong. All four headings are present, with the correct clause number and the correct title, spelled exactly as printed. No text of the standard is lost, altered, reflowed away, or mis-transcribed anywhere on this page. Every list item under them matches the PDF verbatim as well. The sole defect is the count of '#' characters. (b) THE PDF CARRIES NO HEADING LEVELS TO CONTRADICT. Looking at the printed glyphs myself across pages 1004, 1005, 1006 and 1009: 'A.4 Optional language element list', 'A.4.1 General', 'A.4.2 ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling', 'A.4.3 Commit and Rollback', 'A.4.4 Dynamic capacity tables', 'A.4.12 RESUME statement', 'A.4.14 VALIDATE' are ALL set in the identical bold face, at the identical size, on the identical left margin. The PDF gives the parent A.4 no typographic distinction whatsoever from its children. The claim's premise - that A.4.4-A.4.7 are 'printed in the same subsection style as A.4.1' and therefore visibly subordinate - is only half true: they are also printed in the same style as A.4 itself. In this standard the hierarchy is carried ENTIRELY by the decimal numbering, and the decimal numbering is transcribed perfectly. Any consumer that derives the tree from the clause number - which is what every citation in this project does ('13.18.38', '9.1.15', '14.9.39') - gets the correct parentage. (c) IT IS A FILE-WIDE PIPELINE ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-1006 DEFECT. The claim presents 'A.4.3 through A.4.11' as an anomalous local run. It is not local. The transcription pipeline systematically assigns the correct deeper level to the first one or two children of a parent and then collapses every later sibling to '##'. The same signature appears everywhere: - '### 8.1.1', '### 8.1.2', then '## 8.1.3', '## 8.1.4', '## 8.1.5' - '### 9.1', '#### 9.1.1', '#### 9.1.2', then '## 9.1.3', '## 9.1.4' ... - '### 12.4.1', '### 12.4.2', '### 12.4.3', then flattening - '## 13.18', '### 13.18.1', then '## 13.18.2' ... '## 13.18.11' ... - '## 14.9', '### 14.9.1', then '## 14.9.2' ... '## 14.9.7' ... - and in Annex A itself: '### A.1 ...', then '## A.2', '## A.3', '## A.4' - i.e. A.2/A.3/A.4 are ALREADY peers of '## Annex A' by the claim's own logic, one level above the headings it complains about. Counted mechanically: 556 numbered headings in specs/ISO_COBOL.md have numbering depth >= 3 yet are emitted at '##', against 1338 emitted at '###' or deeper. A.4.4-A.4.7 are four of those 556. Filing them as a page-1006 discrepancy misattributes a global artifact to one page and, applied consistently, would produce hundreds of duplicate per-page findings for the identical root cause. (d) BY THE REJECTION CRITERIA. The difference is purely presentational encoding in the transcription, it changes no meaning, it drops no text, and it misdescribes the source. That falls squarely under 'the difference is only ... formatting'. If the owner does want the heading tree normalized, the correct remedy is a single mechanical file-wide pass that derives the markdown level from the clause-number depth for all 556 headings plus the annex-letter headings - one change set against the transcription pipeline, not a page-1006 spec-reconciliation ledger entry.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. All four headings (A.4.4, A.4.5, A.4.6, A.4.7) are present on page 1006 with the correct clause number and correct title, and every list item beneath them matches the PDF verbatim; nothing is missing, so kind='missing-heading' is incorrect. The observation that they are emitted at '##' is accurate, but (i) the PDF prints A.4 and ALL of A.4.1-A.4.14 in one identical bold face at one identical size and margin, so the PDF supplies no level distinction for the markdown to contradict - hierarchy there is carried solely by the decimal numbering, which is transcribed exactly; and (ii) the flattening is a global transcription-pipeline behaviour, not a page-1006 defect: the pipeline keeps the correct level for a parent's first child or two and collapses later siblings to '##', producing 556 numbered headings of depth >= 3 emitted at '##' across the file (8.1.3+, 9.1.3+, 13.18.2+, 14.9.2+, and in Annex A the parents '## A.2', '## A.3', '## A.4' themselves, which are already peers of '## Annex A'). Any heading-level normalization should be one mechanical file-wide pass over all 556, not a per-page reconciliation finding.
